cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! I'm so happy to see you again.

cues.caption: Last time: count the sides, name the shape
cues.text: Last time, you named shapes just by counting their sides. Triangle, three. Square, four. Hexagon, six!

cues.caption: Chapter 2 · Grids and Coordinates
cues.text: Today is chapter two of Shapes, Grids, and Coordinates. It's called, Grids and Coordinates!

cues.caption: Find any spot, like a treasure map!
cues.text: By the end, you'll be able to find any spot on a grid, just like reading a treasure map!

cues.caption: Aarav and Diya on the tiled terrace
cues.text: Remember Aarav? Today he's playing on the terrace with his little sister, Diya. The floor is covered in square tiles, rows and rows of them.

cues.caption: Diya: "Your ball is at (4, 2)!"
cues.text: Diya hides Aarav's cricket ball, and gives him a clue. Your ball is at, four, two!

cues.caption: 2 across, 4 up… no ball!
cues.text: Aarav starts at the corner. He walks two tiles across, then four tiles up. He looks down. No ball! Oh no.

cues.caption: He used both numbers. What went wrong?
cues.text: Hmm. He used both numbers. So why didn't he find the ball? Think about it.

cues.caption: 4 across first, then 2 up. Found it!
cues.text: He used them in the wrong order! Diya meant four across first, then two up. And there's the ball! The order of the numbers really matters.

cues.caption: Grid = lines going across and up
cues.text: Aarav's tiled floor is a grid. A grid is made of lines going across, and lines going up. Just like a chessboard!

cues.caption: Rows go side to side · columns stand tall
cues.text: The lines make rows, that go side to side, and columns, that stand up tall. A chessboard has eight rows, and eight columns.

cues.caption: Start at (0, 0), the origin, bottom left
cues.text: Every grid needs a starting point. It's the bottom left corner, and we call it, zero, zero. It has a special name too, the origin.

cues.caption: Coordinates = a point's address, like (4, 2)
cues.text: Every point on a grid has an address, called its coordinates. We write two numbers inside brackets, like four, two.

cues.caption: 1st number: how far across (x)
cues.text: The first number tells you how far to go across, to the right. Its short name is x.

cues.caption: 2nd number: how far up (y)
cues.text: The second number tells you how far to go up. Its short name is y.

cues.caption: (4, 2): 4 across, then 2 up
cues.text: So, to reach four, two, start at zero, zero. Walk four across. One, two, three, four. Then climb two up. One, two. You're there!

cues.caption: Walk along, then climb up: across, then up!
cues.text: Here's a trick to remember it. Walk along the floor, before you climb the stairs. Across first, then up!

cues.caption: (4, 2) and (2, 4) are different places!
cues.text: Watch what happens when we swap the numbers. Four, two, is here. But two, four, means two across, and four up. That's a totally different spot!

cues.caption: In (3, 5), which number is across?
cues.text: Quick question. In the address three, five, which number tells you how far to go across? Think.

cues.caption: 3 is across, 5 is up
cues.text: Three! The first number is always across. And five is up.

cues.caption: From (0, 0): 2 across, 3 up. Address?
cues.text: Your turn. Start at zero, zero. Go two across, and three up. What's your address? Pause, and think.

cues.caption: (2, 3)! Across first, then up
cues.text: Two, three! The across number goes first, and the up number goes second.

cues.caption: (1, 2) → 3 right → (4, 2)
cues.text: Now let's move around! Aarav is at one, two. He moves three steps to the right. Moving right adds to the across number. One plus three is four. So now he's at four, two.

cues.caption: (4, 1) → 2 up → (4, 3)
cues.text: Diya is at four, one. She moves two steps up. Moving up adds to the up number. One plus two is three. So she's at four, three!

cues.caption: (5, 3) → 1 left → (4, 3)
cues.text: And moving left takes away from the across number. From five, three, one step left takes you to, four, three.

cues.caption: (2, 2): 3 right, 2 up, 1 left. Where now?
cues.text: Here's a tricky one! Start at two, two. Move three right, then two up, then one left. Where do you end up? Take your time.

cues.caption: (5, 2) → (5, 4) → (4, 4)!
cues.text: Step by step. Three right takes you to five, two. Two up takes you to five, four. One left takes you to, four, four!

cues.caption: (1, 1) → (1, 5): it moved 4 up
cues.text: And if a chess piece moves from one, one, to one, five? The across number stays the same. The up number goes from one to five. So it moved four up!

cues.caption: Battleship on a 5 × 5 grid!
cues.text: Game time! Let's play battleship. Aarav hides a ship on a five by five grid, and Diya has to guess where it is.

cues.caption: The ship hides at (3, 4)
cues.text: Shh, don't tell Diya. The ship is hiding at three, four. Three across, four up.

cues.caption: Diya guesses (4, 3). Hit or miss?
cues.text: Diya guesses four, three. Is that a hit, or a miss? Think!

cues.caption: (4, 3) → Miss! The numbers are swapped
cues.text: Splash, it's a miss! Four, three, is a different spot. The numbers are swapped.

cues.caption: (3, 4) → Hit! Across, then up
cues.text: Then she guesses three, four. Boom! A hit! So always read the address carefully. Across, then up.

cues.caption: A screen is a giant grid of pixels
cues.text: Guess what? Computers use grids too! A screen is a giant grid of tiny squares, called pixels.

cues.caption: Each pixel has an address, like (120, 45)
cues.text: Every pixel has its own address, like one hundred and twenty, forty five. The computer uses that address to know exactly which pixel to colour.

cues.caption: Colour the right pixels → a picture!
cues.text: Colour the right pixels, and a picture appears! That's how every game and cartoon gets onto your screen.

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, practice check time, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Mark (4, 2). Which number is across?
cues.text: Mark four, two on a grid. Which number is across? Pause the video, and try it on paper.

cues.caption: 4 is across: 4 across, then 2 up
cues.text: Four is across! Start at zero, zero. Go four across, then two up, and mark your point. Did you get it? Brilliant!

cues.caption: A grid has rows and columns
cues.text: Let's remember. A grid has rows and columns.

cues.caption: Address = (across, up)
cues.text: An address is two numbers. Across, then up.

cues.caption: Across first, then up. Order matters!
cues.text: Across first, then up. The order matters!

cues.caption: Screens are grids of pixels
cues.text: And screens are giant grids of pixels.

cues.caption: Chapter 2 done!
cues.text: Chapter two, done! You can find any point on a grid now, champ.

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
